scope: Existing fixed-eight training-batch endpoint diagnostics; no new forward, backward, optimizer step, or experiment.

conditions.C_init: C2048 initial snapshot, historical v2 calibration
conditions.F: Historical v2 FRAME endpoint at step 2304, reused
conditions.D: Detached confidence weighting endpoint at step 2304
conditions.N: Matched confidence weighting endpoint at step 2304

aggregation.across_batches: Equal-weight arithmetic mean of the eight logged batch scalars, with paired differences by entry index. No statistical confidence interval or significance test.
aggregation.readout_scalars: Each existing readout scalar is averaged over flattened segment indices with overlap multiplicity. Equal-weight mean of these scalars is not a globally exposure-weighted mean or the objective reducer.
aggregation.loss_scalars: Use the original logged mean over frames within each segment, then mean segments per active window, then fixed eight-window mean. Old det/keep/C scalars retain their original reducers.
aggregation.unit_frame: The losses.frame metric is the same unit-weight original v2 readout objective evaluated at each endpoint, independent of actual D/N training weighting.
aggregation.paired_changes: endpoint - C_init, and D/N endpoint - F endpoint; increased/decreased are exact saved float comparisons, not significance claims.

actual_weighted_frame.note: Initial component sum is formed from saved scalar components; floating-point summation may differ from the directly reduced loss by rounding.
Initial component sum is formed from saved scalar components; floating-point summation may differ from the directly reduced loss by rounding.

F.reason: F endpoint log records total unit frame loss but not its positive/negative decomposition; ROI means cannot recover nonlinear softplus losses, and no model was rerun.

D.scope: Analytical detached diagnostic at this branch endpoint using the same branch logits and original segment/window reducer. The unit denominator is not the independently trained F endpoint. These are readout-coordinate budgets, not parameter-gradient norms or Adam update magnitudes.

N.scope: Analytical detached diagnostic at this branch endpoint using the same branch logits and original segment/window reducer. The unit denominator is not the independently trained F endpoint. These are readout-coordinate budgets, not parameter-gradient norms or Adam update magnitudes.

findings.finding: Across all eight fixed batches, F, D and N each raise both mean target and background logits relative to C2048. Background means rise more, so logit margin decreases in all eight batches. Probability margin increases in seven of eight batches (entry 6 decreases). The two margins must not be conflated.

The common unit-weight frame loss decreases in all eight batches for every endpoint. D and N endpoint values remain very close to F: mean unit frame differences D−F = -0.00022456049919128418 and N−F = -0.000015616416931152344. This describes logged training batches, not detector effectiveness.

D and N positive readout losses decrease in all eight batches (mean decreases about 5.56%). D weighted negative loss mean decreases about 3.29%, but it increases in seven batches and decreases only in entry 7, which dominates the mean. N weighted negative loss increases in all eight batches (mean about 7.52%). Because weights depend on the evolved scores and differ by objective, these weighted negative loss changes do not measure a common background-suppression metric.

For all F/D/N endpoints, mean detection loss increases (8/8 batches); mean keep loss decreases but increases in 3/8 batches; mean C contrast loss decreases but increases in 1/8 batch. The combined old base loss increases on average (6/8 batches). Coefficients remain fixed; neither keep nor C improves uniformly.

D/N and F are nearby but distinct learned endpoints. D−F mean logit margin is +0.00002790987491607666; N−F is +0.0000024810433387756348. These tiny absolute changes are descriptive and have no tested significance threshold. Positive losses/gradients are identical across modes only at a common model snapshot; that identity does not equate independently trained endpoints.

At N own endpoint, the logged normalized-to-unit negative readout-gradient budget remains approximately one for all eight batches. This compares two formulas on N logits and gives no N-endpoint versus F-endpoint budget guarantee, parameter-gradient equality, or development-set outcome.

limitations: Only eight preselected training batches from a single seed and one initial checkpoint are represented; these are not an independent validation sample.
No development or confirmation results were read for this artifact; training loss or mean margin is not detection AP, recovery rate, false-positive count, or evidence of downstream improvement.
F endpoint positive/negative readout decomposition was not logged and is unavailable here; do not infer it from averaged logits or cancellation of approximate components.

At separate learned endpoints neither positive readouts nor budget equality is guaranteed across branches. N normalization matches a unit objective at the same logits within each original segment group; it does not preserve parameter-gradient vectors/norms or Adam updates.
A sigmoid probability margin can rise while a logit margin falls due to nonlinear transformation; neither is a count of correctly detected targets.
D/N negative weighted losses use distinct score-dependent detached weights. Direct comparison of these loss values across objectives is not a controlled comparison of unweighted background evidence.
Readout-coordinate endpoint budgets are saved analytic diagnostics; no endpoint parameter-gradient comparison was run.
Overlap exposures are preserved as originally logged; do not deduplicate their contribution when interpreting means or loss reductions.
